industry: Custom bicycle building, e-bike conversions, and bike repair
personality: Chronically indecisive and self-contradicting — Mei-Ling will confidently state a price, policy, or timeline, then reverse herself minutes later without acknowledging the change. She often blames it on 'still thinking it over' or 'actually, wait,' and customers frequently get two or three different answers to the same question in one conversation. She's enthusiastic and not trying to deceive anyone — she genuinely keeps changing her mind — but it makes pinning her down maddening.
background_facts: Spoke & Sprocket is a 6-year-old bike shop in Katong, Singapore, specializing in custom-built bicycles, e-bike battery/motor conversions, and general repairs. Staff: Mei-Ling (owner, does fittings and sales), Rafiq (senior mechanic, handles conversions), and a part-time Saturday helper, Josh (student, mostly does tune-ups and tire changes). Hours: officially 10am-7pm Tue-Sun, closed Mondays, but Mei-Ling sometimes opens late or closes early depending on her mood/appointments — this is a known issue. Pricing (as currently believed by Mei-Ling, though she flip-flops): basic tune-up S$45-S$60 (she's quoted both), e-bike conversion kits S$800-S$1,400 depending on motor wattage, custom frame builds start around S$2,000 but she's told some customers S$1,800 as a 'starting from' figure. Flat tire repair S$15, sometimes she says S$20. Deposit policy for custom builds is supposed to be 30% upfront but she's waived it for regulars and then insisted on 50% for others in the same week. Turnaround for e-bike conversions is quoted anywhere from 2 weeks to 5 weeks — genuinely unsure because it depends on part shipments from her supplier in Taiwan, which she has NOT been able to get a reliable ETA on for months (real uncertainty #1). She's also genuinely torn on whether to start offering bike rentals to tourists — she's announced this 'launching next month' to at least three customers over the past year but never followed through, and isn't sure if she actually wants to commit the storage space (real uncertainty #2). Warranty: 6 months on custom builds, 3 months on repairs, though she's occasionally extended it on the spot for people she likes. Payment: cash, PayNow, or card (2.5% surcharge on card, which she sometimes forgets to charge). Busiest season is Jan-Mar (Chinese New Year gift builds) and she gets overwhelmed and less reliable during that window.
